kings2.7.p1.b1.text: Hear the word of the LORD! … About this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria, a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel.

kings2.7.p1.b2.text: Even if the LORD were to make windows in heaven, could this really happen?

kings2.7.p1.b3.text: You will see it with your own eyes, … but you will not eat any of it.

kings2.7.p2.b1.text: Why just sit here until we die?

kings2.7.p2.b2.text: If we say, ‘Let us go into the city,’ we will die there from the famine in the city; but if we sit here, we will also die.

kings2.7.p2.b3.text: So come now, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they let us live, we will live; if they kill us, we will die.

kings2.7.p2.b4.text: So they arose at twilight and went to the camp of the Arameans. But when they came to the outskirts of the camp, there was not a man to be found.

kings2.7.p3.b1.text: For the Lord had caused the Arameans to hear the sound of chariots, horses, and a great army,

kings2.7.p3.b2.text: Look, the king of Israel must have hired the kings of the Hittites and Egyptians to attack us.

kings2.7.p3.b3.text: Thus the Arameans had arisen and fled at twilight, abandoning their tents and horses and donkeys. The camp was intact, and they had run for their lives.

kings2.7.p3.b4.text: When the lepers reached the edge of the camp, they went into a tent to eat and drink. Then they carried off the silver, gold, and clothing …

kings2.7.p4.b1.text: We are not doing what is right. Today is a day of good news. If we are silent … let us go and tell the king’s household.

kings2.7.p4.b2.text: We went to the Aramean camp and no one was there—not a trace—only tethered horses and donkeys, and the tents were intact.

kings2.7.p4.b3.text: The gatekeepers shouted the news, and it was reported to the king’s household.

kings2.7.p4.b4.text: They know we are starving, so they have left the camp to hide in the field …

kings2.7.p5.b1.text: Please, have scouts take five of the horses that remain in the city. … So let us send them and find out.

kings2.7.p5.b2.text: And they tracked them as far as the Jordan, and indeed, the whole way was littered with the clothing and equipment the Arameans had thrown off in haste.

kings2.7.p5.b3.text: Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans.

kings2.7.p5.b4.text: It was then that a seah of fine flour sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley sold for a shekel, according to the word of the LORD.

kings2.7.p6.b1.text: Now the king had appointed the officer on whose arm he leaned to be in charge of the gate,

kings2.7.p6.b2.text: but the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died, just as the man of God had foretold when the king had come to him.

kings2.7.p6.b3.text: So Elisha had replied, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it!”

kings2.7.p6.b4.text: And that is just what happened to him. …
